claims.text: The initial material is as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Replacing Mo with Nb or Ti will reduce the density of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Replacing Mo with Nb or Ti will preserve the alloy's room-temperature mechanical performance.
Replacing Mo with Nb or Ti will preserve the alloy's high-temperature mechanical performance.
Substitution of a heavy element by a lighter refractory element lowers overall alloy density.
The substitution may retain a favorable microstructure.
Retention of a favorable microstructure and solid-solution strengthening may maintain mechanical properties after substitution.
The modified alloy is predicted to have a density 5–10% lower than as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The modified alloy is predicted to retain room-temperature yield strength above 1500 MPa.
The modified alloy is predicted to retain yield strength above 800 MPa at 1000 °C.
The modified alloy is predicted to have room-temperature fracture toughness of at least 20 MPa m^1/2.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of about 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has an elevated-temperature yield strength of 855 MPa.
The relevant temperature boundary extends from room temperature to 1600 °C.
The hypothesis is rejected if density reduction is less than 3%.
The hypothesis is rejected if room-temperature yield strength falls below 1200 MPa.
The hypothesis is rejected if yield strength at 1000 °C falls below 700 MPa.
The hypothesis is rejected if room-temperature fracture toughness falls below 15 MPa m^1/2.

contradictions.description: The requested intervention is presented as single, but the hypothesis permits either Nb or Ti and the experiment proposes multiple unspecified substitution proportions, so no single composition-level intervention is defined.

The predicted maintenance thresholds are 1500 MPa, 800 MPa, and 20 MPa m^1/2, whereas rejection occurs only below 1200 MPa, 700 MPa, and 15 MPa m^1/2. Thus substantial failure to meet the stated prediction would not falsify the hypothesis under the proposed rule.
The stated boundary extends to 1600 °C, but the experiment tests mechanical performance only at room temperature and 1000 °C, leaving the claimed upper-temperature range untested.
